newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: A consistent stream of offshore dollar demand saw the South African rand end more than two-and-a-half cents weaker on the dollar but forex traders said it was difficult to justify the demand for the U.S. unit.
The rand closed at 4.6840/6890 on the dollar after a steady start and from 4.6570/6620 at Friday's close. It hit a low bid of 4.6865 during the day.
"One possible reason (for the buying) is that foreigners were unimpressed with the weekend violence at Impala Platinum's Widebeestfontein mine," a senior forex trader said.
"Other than that there has been no bad news...fundamentaly the rand should be stronger, especially after the higher than expected reserves number on Friday," he added.
Violence in a squatter camp adjoining Impala's Wildebeestfontein South mine near Rustenberg claimed 37 lives at the weekend.

South Africa's gold and foreign exchange reserves rose to 10.93 billion rand in November from October's 10.28 billion rand, the Reserve Bank said on Friday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast November reserves at 10.38 billion rand, with the range 10.0 to 11.0 billion rand.
Forex traders said the rand was looking fundamentally strong and many were surprised at the two-and-a-half cents loss on the day.
"The London and New York guys are aware of the fact that it's not clever to sit short (on dollars) but we were nonetheless surprised at today's moves," one said.
He said a test of the higher 4.7000/7050 levels was possible over the next few days but he expected the rand to run into resistance at around 4.7050.
Against the crosses, the rand was last quoted at 7.7099/7204 against sterling from 7.6591/6697 previously and at 0.3314/3319 marks from 0.3296/3300 marks on Friday.

Bonds started the day stronger on the back of the better reserves number and a recovery in U.S. Treasuries after panic sales on Friday prompted by remarks by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.
But the market pared intraday gains after profit-taking set in and the rand ticked weaker.
At 1421 GMT government's benchmark R150 stock was trading at a 15.935 percent yield from 15.97 percent on Friday.
"There was good demand initially on the better reserves figure and the recovery on the U.S. market. In addition, the market was caught slightly short on Friday," a bond trader said.
But he said profit-taking and the weaker rand forced yields progressively higher during the day.
Traders predicted a 15.82 to 16.00 percent range for the rest of the week with the market looking towards the rand for direction in the absence of fresh economic indicators.
Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners were net buyers of local bonds to the tune of 19.05 million rand on Friday after buying 47.88 million rand on Thursday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 4.72 billion rand on Friday from 37.16 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement date.
On the money market, three-month NCD rates were steady at between 17.15 and 17.20 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also quoted unchanged in a 16.50 to 16.75 percent range.
The Reserve Bank indicated the money market shortage at 8.761 billion rand on Saturday from 8.798 billion rand on Friday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
